The header states the reading: "Equipped with the logical connectives below it is a bicartesian closed thin category — a Heyting prealgebra ... The exponential is implication because cartesian closure is exactly the adjunction (R ∧ P) ⊢ Q ↔ R ⊢ (P → Q), the deduction theorem."
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: the 'lattice as a thin CCC' content is carried out for exactly ONE preorder — Coq's `Prop` under implication, a Heyting PREalgebra. That preorder does coincide with P(U) at U = a singleton (subsets of a point = truth values), so a degenerate instance of (a) is in the tree, but P(U) for a general U is never constructed, no Boolean algebra is ever constructed, and there is no general theorem 'a preorder with finite meets and relative pseudo-complements is cartesian closed', which is the actual content of both halves.

gap: Neither half is instantiated as stated. Only the U = singleton case is effectively present, as `Props`. (b) No Boolean-algebra structure exists in-tree at all; the one concrete two-element Boolean algebra `_2` (Instance/Two.v) is given Cartesian + Terminal (Instance/Two/Monoidal.v:80, 98) but no `Closed` instance, and Instance/Two.v:85-89 only remarks in prose that "a Heyting algebra is a skeletal thin finitely-cocomplete cartesian-closed category, and a Boolean algebra a skeletal thin finitely-cocomplete star-autonomous one". evidence.intree_statement: Program Definition Props : Category := {| obj := Prop; hom := Basics.impl; homset := fun P Q => {| equiv := fun f g => True |}; id := fun _ x => x; compose := fun _ _ _ g f x => g (f x) |}.

"Objects are propositions (`Prop`) and a morphism P ~> Q is an implication ... this is a thin / posetal category: at most one arrow between any two objects, so P ~> Q is inhabited exactly when P entails Q. That makes Props the preorder of propositions ordered by implication. ... 1 = True, 0 = False, P × Q = P ∧ Q, P + Q = P ∨ Q, Q ^ P = P → Q ... The exponential is implication because cartesian closure is exactly the adjunction (R ∧ P) ⊢ Q ↔ R ⊢ (P → Q), the deduction theorem."

Program Instance Props_Closed : @Closed Props _ := { exponent_obj := Basics.impl; exp_iso := fun _ _ _ => {| to := {| morphism := fun f a b => f (conj a b) |} ; from := {| morphism := fun f p => f (proj1 p) (proj2 p) |} |} }.

(* Forward mate: paste η' on the left, whisker σ, paste ε on the right. *)
Definition mate (σ : (f' ∘∘∘ a) ~> (b ∘∘∘ f)) : (a ∘∘∘ u) ~> (u' ∘∘∘ b) :=
  postcomp_to Af (from (hassoc u' b f) ∘∘ precomp_to Af' σ).   (* Context: Af : BicatAdjunction f u, Af' : BicatAdjunction f' u', a : bicat x x', b : bicat y y' *)

Definition mate_inv (τ : (a ∘∘∘ u) ~> (u' ∘∘∘ b)) : (f' ∘∘∘ a) ~> (b ∘∘∘ f) :=
  precomp_from Af' (to (hassoc u' b f) ∘∘ postcomp_from Af τ).

Theorem Cat_mate_unfold_raw (Z : y) :
  transform[mate Af Af' σ] Z
    ≈ fmap[U'] (fmap[b] (adj_counit F U Z))
        ∘ (fmap[U'] (σ (fobj[U] Z)) ∘ adj_unit F' U' (fobj[a] (fobj[U] Z))).   (* the classical conjugate formula, componentwise, in Cat *)

Definition mate_dom : SetoidObject := {| carrier := (f' ∘∘∘ a) ~{bicat x y'}~> (b ∘∘∘ f) |}.
Definition mate_cod : SetoidObject := {| carrier := (a ∘∘∘ u) ~{bicat y x'}~> (u' ∘∘∘ b) |}.
Program Definition mate_iso : @Isomorphism Sets mate_dom mate_cod := {| to := {| morphism := mate |}; from := {| morphism := mate_inv |} |}.
Lemma mate_roundtrip_left (σ : (f' ∘∘∘ a) ~> (b ∘∘∘ f)) : mate_inv (mate σ) ≈ σ.
Lemma mate_roundtrip_right (τ : (a ∘∘∘ u) ~> (u' ∘∘∘ b)) : mate (mate_inv τ) ≈ τ.

Theorem Cat_mate_unfold (Z : y) :
  transform[mate Af Af' σ] Z
    ≈ fmap[U'] (fmap[b] (adj_counit F U Z)) ∘ to adj[Cat_BicatAdjunction_Adjunction Af'] (σ (fobj[U] Z)).   (* the mate as the transpose ⌊σ (U Z)⌋ post-whiskered by the counit: characterization (i), in Cat *)

Lemma mate_charac {a b : bicat y x} (Aa : BicatAdjunction f a) (Ab : BicatAdjunction f b) (γ : a ~> b) :
  rwhisker γ f ∘∘ uη Aa ≈ uη Ab → γ ≈ matecell Aa Ab.   (* the unit characterization, only in the special case of two right adjoints of ONE 1-cell f, i.e. F = F' and σ = id *)

statement_record.book: For two adjunctions between X and A, σ : F ⟹ F' and τ : G' ⟹ G are conjugate iff any one of four diagrams commutes: (i) τ = G ε' ∘ G σ G' ∘ η G'; (ii) σ = ε F' ∘ F τ F' ∘ F η'; (iii) ε ∘ F τ = ε' ∘ σ G'; (iv) G σ ∘ η = τ F' ∘ η'. Moreover each σ has a unique conjugate τ and each τ a unique conjugate σ — a bijection between the two sets of natural transformations.
statement_record.intree: `mate_iso : @Isomorphism Sets mate_dom mate_cod`, with `mate_roundtrip_left : mate_inv (mate σ) ≈ σ` and `mate_roundtrip_right : mate (mate_inv τ) ≈ τ`, over an arbitrary bicategory B, two internal adjunctions f ⊣ u and f' ⊣ u', and 1-cells a, b. `mate` is defined BY the pasting composite (Mac Lane's (i)) and `mate_inv` by the dual pasting (his (ii)); in Cat the composite unfolds to the classical formula (`Cat_mate_unfold`).
